Hi Priya —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Per our conversation, attached is the concurrency profile we see in production (sampled): orion-concurrency-profile.csv. The key asks from our side before we greenlight the onboarding test run:

- We need a night-run (off-peak) to validate sustained throughput at our expected peaks (we expect burst windows at 18:00 UTC).
- Clear acceptance criteria for latency (p95/p99), error rate, and cost delta from baseline.
- Proof that KV cache warming and prefix caching works across replica restarts.

Can you propose a test schedule (dates/times in UTC) and a short checklist of required artifacts we should prepare? Also, we'll need the output evidence (logs/traces) in a location we can download after the run.

Thanks — looking to get this finished this week if possible.

—Ethan

Hi Ethan —

Thanks for the file — that profile is helpful. Proposed plan below (concise):

1) Acceptance criteria (summary)
   - P95 latency: <= 200 ms (inference-only path, end-to-end p95 <= 350 ms)
   - P99 latency: <= 500 ms (inference-only)
   - Sustained throughput target: 600 requests/sec at 75% request mix (your avg payload)
   - Error budget: < 0.5% errors (5xx / model-failure) during steady-state window
   - Memory/cold-start checks: KV cache hit rate >= 85% after warm-up period

2) Concurrency matrix to validate (steady-state durations shown):
   - 50 concurrent clients, 30 minutes steady-state
   - 200 concurrent clients, 60 minutes steady-state
   - 500 concurrent clients, 90 minutes steady-state (night-run target)

3) Night-run scheduling (UTC)
   - Proposed night-run: 2025-11-05 01:00–04:00 UTC (covers your 18:00 burst window in the US)
   - Warm-up: first 20 minutes (ramping), then steady-state windows as above

4) Instrumentation & evidence we will capture
   - Per-request traces (sampling at 100%), per-route token-level cost logs, per-token latency breakdowns
   - GPU utilization + kernel telemetry snapshots every 60s
   - Rolling error logs and per-model reject reasons

5) Rollback / fail criteria
   - Abort if p95 doubles expected threshold or error rate > 1.5% for > 5 minutes
   - Auto-fallback to compatible lower-latency model variant on sustained failures

6) Artifacts we need from Orion before run
   - Confirmed test traffic token set (anon), typical payload size, and sample user IDs
   - Any proxy or IP allowlist details so we can ensure routing to your instance

I've attached our load plan (redwood-load-plan-v1.pdf) and a short tracing config snippet (tracing-config-snippet.txt) showing how to ingest the traces you asked for.

Next steps: if that schedule works, Ben will open the evidence transfer folder and we'll provide upload credentials; Marcus will coordinate the test harness and confirm the exact request mix.

Best,

Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
